name: BEC / Email Compromise
description: Business Email Compromise — account takeover, mail-rule manipulation, wire fraud.
initialKeyQuestions: How was initial access achieved (phishing, password spray, OAuth grant)?
Were mail-forwarding rules or inbox rules created by the attacker?
Were financial transactions or wire transfers initiated?
What external IP addresses and user-agents accessed the account?
Was MFA present and, if so, how was it bypassed?
What data was accessed or exfiltrated from the mailbox?

initialNextSteps.action: Revoke all active sessions and reset the compromised account's password and MFA
initialNextSteps.pointer: Entra ID → Revoke sessions, reset MFA, reset password

initialNextSteps.action: Export the Unified Audit Log (UAL) for all affected mailboxes (past 90 days)
initialNextSteps.rationale: Primary evidence source for all mailbox and sign-in activity
initialNextSteps.pointer: Microsoft Purview compliance portal → Audit search

initialNextSteps.action: Review and immediately delete any attacker-created inbox rules
initialNextSteps.rationale: Inbox rules hide replies and forward mail to attacker-controlled addresses

initialNextSteps.action: Audit OAuth app grants and newly consented applications on the compromised account
initialNextSteps.rationale: OAuth grants survive password resets and provide persistent mailbox access
initialNextSteps.pointer: Entra ID → Enterprise Applications → User consent

synthesisHint: This is a BEC case — prioritize T1566 Phishing (initial access), T1098 Account Manipulation (inbox rules / OAuth grants), T1078 Valid Accounts, and T1567 Exfiltration to Cloud Service.
